observed_gap: Seventy native blocked events were local Pump.fun cooldown/window waits, but all used provider_quota and a fixed 5-second queue retry. Original per-token state was unbounded. The configured per-token cooldown was 60 seconds, not the code default of 25 seconds.
implementation: A single process-wide, thread-safe admission owner retains the configured rolling attempt limit and per-token cooldown.
Denials expose exact remaining local wait and distinct token, window, combined, state-capacity, invalid-clock, disabled and invalid-identity reasons.

Native entry defers with entry_observation:local_pumpfun_wait:<reason> before birth or market requests; the queue uses a whole-second ceiling of the remaining wait instead of fixed polling every 5 seconds.

Expired per-token state is swept, live cooldowns cannot be evicted to admit another token, and attempts cannot disappear from a silently truncated 64-item deque. State capacity defaults to 8192; the configured attempt count is bounded at 4096.

A first attempt at monotonic zero is not mistaken for a previous attempt. Invalid, backwards or unrepresentable clocks deny admission without refreshing original state. Invalid optional settings have safe importable defaults; explicit zero/nonpositive integer attempt quotas remain disabled and fractional seconds are supported.
Safe aggregate runtime diagnostics contain no token identities, endpoints or credentials. They explicitly do not claim wire quota, provider entitlement or buy permission.
preserved: Configured 4 attempts per 10 seconds and 60-second operator per-token cooldown; operator .env is unchanged.
Original queue first_seen, mint creation context, immutable feature/quote requirements, queue expiry and retry budget.
All entry/risk/activation thresholds, exact 0.1 SOL sizing and uncapped runner exits.
Missing or stale provider data remains unknown; no fallback manufactures mint age, liquidity, financial labels or profitable trades.
All original scope, historical evidence and ten remaining whole-goal requirements.
queue_wakeup_bound: Normal finite waits round up, never down. Extreme configured waits are rechecked at most hourly while the monotonic admission owner still enforces the original expiry; a wake-up is not admission.

baseline.source: Exact published parent native functions, independently AST-extracted without importing the operational bot
proved: Invented initial cooldown at monotonic zero
Configured 100-attempt window admits attempt 101 because the deque retains only 64
Native deferral cannot schedule a supplied remaining wait
baseline.qualification: The high-quota and zero-clock cases are software reproductions, not established causes of the operator's last zero-buy run.

tests.scope: Pure local admission, concurrent callers, bounded retention, disabled/invalid settings, exact boundaries, actual native entry prefix before mocked birth/market calls, original legacy queue requeue and runtime stats binding. No operational provider call, model training or bot launch.
tests.initial_test_expectation_correction: Initial targeted run was 1 failed/366 passed: the new test incorrectly treated fractional seconds as invalid. It now distinguishes valid fractional seconds from an invalid fractional attempt count; no production limit was weakened to satisfy that test.

The local wait telemetry does not distinguish historical token versus window branches retrospectively.
The native forced-tree stop remains a separate lifecycle issue; this scanner change does not claim to fix graceful shutdown.
